A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cEBMF research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations, MovieLens prediction results, spatial transcriptomics analyses, and runtime measurements, including additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation, MovieLens, spatial transcriptomics, and scalability results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The modeling framework and cEBNM reduction are retained. However, the printed update schedule changes: v1 Algorithms 1 and 3 update residual precision during every single-factor update, whereas v2 Algorithm 1 updates it once before each sweep over factors. Greedy initialization remains described in prose.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four simulation scenarios, MovieLens 100K, all 12 DLPFC slices, and scalability experiments spanning 1,000 to one million rows. The appendix noise levels are retained; reorganizing their figures introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Reported comparator coverage narrows in the shifted-clustering noise sweep: Spatial PCA appears in v1 Figure 8's mean/interval panels but is absent from v2 Figure 8, although it remains in main Figure 2. The principal comparator families otherwise persist. Spatial PCA's appearance in v2's main tiled-clustering panel redisplays a comparison already present in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: Important reported settings change. Spatial cEBNMF goes from K fixed by manual annotations and EBNMF at K=5 in v1 Appendix C.6 to adaptive ranks capped at 20 and 50, respectively, in v2 Section 4.3. Tiled-clustering cEBMF mixture weights change from an MLP description to multinomial regression, while the EBMF loading prior changes from point-exponential to mixture-of-exponentials. These are substantive specification revisions; the PDFs do not establish rerunning the experiments.

E4.justification: The uninformative-covariate, misspecified-prior, noise-sensitivity, and spatial case analyses remain. However, removing baseline-specific outcomes from the shifted-clustering noise sweep reduces the robustness evidence for those methods. No new ablation or robustness question is introduced.

E5.justification: v2 removes all appendix mean-and-95%-confidence-interval panels and their normal-error calculation descriptions, retaining boxplots. Figure 3 changes the reported MovieLens repetitions from 30 random training/test splits to 10. The conflicting v1 Appendix C.4 statement of 400 simulations also disappears, leaving the retained 100-simulation description. These are substantial reporting changes, without proof that run counts actually changed.

E6.justification: Some detailed shifted-clustering noise-sweep outcomes disappear, as does v1's reported Spatial PCA memory requirement exceeding 3.7 TB at one million rows. Every runtime value in Table 1 is retained, and the main empirical conclusions remain broadly stable. The revision does not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The same lemma and factor-update proposition remain, with added common/row-specific variance formulas and conditional computational-complexity estimates. v2 corrects Gaussian-quadratic signs and the main-text least-squares update. However, its appendix equations (23–24) introduce division by s squared, contradicting that update, and equation (30) replaces v1's posterior second moment with a squared posterior mean. These are mathematical changes beyond equivalent rewriting.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a flexible empirical Bayes factorization framework incorporating side information through learned priors, competitive empirical performance, and scalability. The added implementation-access statement does not redefine the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies expert spatial annotations as a reference rather than definitive ground truth and explains that inferred structures may be previously unknown. It also conjectures that deep-learning comparators could benefit from larger MovieLens datasets and explains that comparator scalability constrained dataset selection. These qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Reproducibility documentation changes substantially. Supplementary-ZIP access instructions become separate implementation and experiment repository links, and v2 discloses an ELBO stopping rule and a 20-iteration scalability cap. Conversely, it removes simulation training/batch details, the spatial-normalization tutorial reference, and the HPC allocations and wall-time budgets documented in v1 Appendices C.4–C.7. Repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting variational empirical Bayes, coordinate descent, and grade-of-membership interpretation, including Kim et al. (2024), Morgante et al. (2023), and Wright (2015). Some sparse-factorization and rank-selection citations disappear. Positioning relative to MFAI, CMF, and spatial methods remains essentially unchanged; publication updates to retained references are not new related work.

P1.justification: The manuscript receives extensive prose editing and restructuring. Simulations gain a numbered subsection, repeated experimental descriptions are consolidated, and the separate derivation and algorithm appendices become one reorganized methods appendix. A NeurIPS checklist and acknowledgments are added, with widespread caption and terminology revisions.

P2.justification: Multiple displays are substantially redesigned: Figure 1's panels are reordered, Figure 2 becomes a larger two-by-two arrangement, and Figure 4 gains larger spatial maps with explicit legends. Appendix boxplots are enlarged and reordered while mean/interval panels disappear. Table 1 adds a software column, and spatial appendix figures are reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability, figure legibility, code-access documentation, and some mathematical expressions. However, it removes useful reproduction details and introduces appendix update inconsistencies in equations (23–24) and (30), while materially revised experimental specifications are not reconciled with the retained results. Both versions contain technical inconsistencies, and the combination of corrections, new errors, and documentation gains and losses prevents a reliable net-quality judgment.
